own_expecting.share: {a} only wants their nan's soup. so i learned it. three tries. third one passed inspection

own_expecting.text: {name} carried every heavy bag home so {a} did not have to.
own_expecting.share: i carry all the shopping now. {a} carries the list. we're both very important

own_expecting.text: {name} watched {a} balance a bowl of grapes on the bump like a little table.
own_expecting.share: {a} is using the bump as a table now. a bowl of grapes balanced there for ten whole minutes

own_expecting.text: {name} pressed an ear to {a}'s bump and got kicked right in the cheek.
own_expecting.share: put my ear to {a}'s bump and got kicked in the face. fair. i was being nosy

own_expecting.text: {name} hurried to the market for pickled herring when {a}'s craving struck.
own_expecting.share: {a} wants pickled herring. at nine at night. i'm on my way. love is strange

own_expecting.text: {name} helped {a} up off the sofa every evening with great ceremony.
own_expecting.share: helping {a} off the sofa is a two-person event now. we count to three. very dramatic

own_expecting.text: {name} sang lullabies to {a}'s bump until both of them were giggling.
own_expecting.share: sang to {a}'s bump. {a} laughed so hard the baby started kicking. teamwork

own_expecting.text: {name} tied {a}'s shoelaces every morning once bending down got too hard.
own_expecting.share: i tie {a}'s shoes every morning now. basically a royal servant. a happy one

own_expecting.text: {name} stocked the kitchen with every snack {a} might possibly crave.
own_expecting.share: stocked the kitchen with every snack known to humankind for {a}. tonight they wanted cucumber. obviously

own_expecting.text: {name} watched {a}'s bump ripple as the baby turned over.
own_expecting.share: watched the baby roll over inside {a}'s belly. like a little wave. i stared for ages

own_expecting.text: {name} blamed hormones in an argument with {a} exactly once and never again.
own_expecting.share: made the mistake of blaming hormones in an argument with {a}. once. never again. i've learned

own_expecting.text: {name} kept {a} company through a long night when the baby would not stop kicking.
own_expecting.share: the baby kept {a} up all night kicking, so we stayed up and talked till sunrise. not a bad night actually

own_expecting.text: {name} moved the bed downstairs so {a} could skip the stairs at night.
own_expecting.share: moved our bed downstairs so {a} can skip the stairs. we sleep in the front room like lodgers now

own_expecting.text: {name} marvelled at how {a}'s bump seemed to grow overnight.
own_expecting.share: i swear {a}'s bump grew overnight. went to bed, woke up, bigger. magic

own_expecting.text: {name} made {a} breakfast in bed every day for a month.
own_expecting.share: breakfast in bed for {a} every day this month. i'm getting good at eggs. finally

own_expecting.text: {name} brushed {a}'s hair every night while {a} dozed off.
own_expecting.share: brushing {a}'s hair at night now. they're asleep in two minutes. i should charge for this

own_expecting.text: {name} discovered that {a} had developed a deep love for sour pickles.
own_expecting.share: {a} eats pickles like crisps now. three jars this week. the shopkeeper knows us by sight

own_expecting.text: {name} guarded {a}'s afternoon naps and made sure nobody disturbed them.
own_expecting.share: guarding {a}'s nap like a bouncer. nobody gets past. not even the cat

own_expecting.text: {name} felt a tiny hand or foot pressing out from {a}'s bump.
own_expecting.share: something tiny poked out of {a}'s bump today. a hand or a foot. either way, it waved at me

own_expecting.text: {name} rubbed oil into {a}'s aching back every night.
own_expecting.share: nightly back rubs for {a}. they groan like an old door. i think that means it's working

own_expecting.text: {name} learned the hard way that {a} could no longer stand the smell of fried fish.
own_expecting.share: learned the hard way that {a} hates fried fish now. we've aired the house for two days

own_expecting.text: {name} slowed every evening stroll to match {a}'s stately waddle.
own_expecting.share: evening walks with {a} are very slow now. a stately waddle. we get overtaken by snails

own_expecting.text: {name} found {a} asleep in the nursery rocking chair with both hands on the bump.
own_expecting.share: found {a} asleep in the nursery rocking chair, hands on the bump. put a blanket on them and tiptoed out

own_expecting.text: {name} read stories aloud to {a}'s bump every night.
own_expecting.share: bedtime stories for {a}'s bump every night. the baby kicks at the good bits. a critic already

own_expecting.text: {name} warmed {a}'s cold feet with a hot water bottle every night.
own_expecting.share: {a}'s feet are always freezing. i'm on hot water bottle duty. very serious job

own_expecting.text: {name} cheered {a} on through a breathing class and did every exercise alongside them.
own_expecting.share: breathing class with {a}. i breathed so hard i got dizzy. {a} was perfectly calm. typical

own_expecting.text: {name} kept a list of every food {a} craved, and it grew stranger every week.
own_expecting.share: keeping a list of {a}'s cravings. this week: lemons, gherkins, and plain rice. very specific baby

own_expecting.text: {name} played a gentle tapping game with the baby through {a}'s bump.
own_expecting.share: tap on {a}'s bump, the baby kicks back. tap again, kick again. playing games already

own_expecting.text: {name} gave up the comfy side of the bed to {a} without a single complaint.
own_expecting.share: gave {a} the comfy side of the bed. permanently. i'm told this is just how it is now

own_expecting.text: {name} baked ginger biscuits to settle {a}'s queasy stomach.
own_expecting.share: baked ginger biscuits for {a}'s queasy tummy. they ate six. i think that means they work

own_expecting.text: {name} carried a spare cushion everywhere in case {a} needed to sit down.
own_expecting.share: i carry a spare cushion everywhere now in case {a} needs to sit. a walking furniture shop

own_expecting.text: {name} teared up the first time {a} guided their hand to feel the baby move.
own_expecting.share: {a} put my hand on the bump and the baby moved. i'm not crying. i'm absolutely crying

own_expecting.text: {name} heard the baby's heartbeat at {a}'s check-up and grinned the whole way home.
own_expecting.share: heard the baby's heartbeat at {a}'s check-up. like a tiny galloping horse. still grinning

own_expecting.text: {name} and {a} brought the family cradle down from the loft and polished it till it shone.
own_expecting.share: The family cradle is down from the loft and polished. {a} says it has rocked four generations.

own_expecting.text: {name} and {a} sat up by the fire talking over names until the candle burned down.
own_expecting.share: Sat up by the fire with {a} talking over names until the candle gave out. We are no nearer.

own_expecting.text: {name} hemmed a stack of little gowns for the baby.
own_expecting.share: I have hemmed six little gowns this week. They are so small I keep holding them up to the light.

own_expecting.text: {name} and {a} whitewashed the small room for the baby.
own_expecting.share: The small room is whitewashed and ready. {a} wears more of it than the walls do.

own_expecting.text: {name}'s mother sent a parcel of knitted things for the baby.
own_expecting.share: My mother has sent a parcel of knitted things. Bonnets, bootees, and a shawl fit for a prince.

own_expecting.text: {name} and {a} walked out on a fine evening and talked about the kind of parents they meant to be.
own_expecting.share: Walked out with {a} this evening and talked about what sort of parents we mean to be. Patient, we decided. We shall see.

own_expecting.text: The midwife came by and told {name} and {a} that all was going well.
own_expecting.share: The midwife came by today and says all is going just as it should. We breathed out for the first time in weeks.

own_expecting.text: {name} and {a} made up the cradle with fresh linen and stood looking at it.
own_expecting.share: Made up the cradle with fresh linen. {a} and I just stood and looked at it for a while.

own_expecting.text: {name}'s neighbors promised to send soup and bread the week the baby came.
own_expecting.share: The neighbors have promised soup and bread the week the baby comes. I could weep, they are so kind.

own_expecting.text: {name} and {a} counted out what they had put by for the baby and found it would do.
own_expecting.share: Counted up what we have put by for the baby. It will do, if we are careful. {a} says we always are.

own_expecting.text: {name} let out the seams of a whole wardrobe of clothes.
own_expecting.share: I have let out the seams of everything I own. Next I shall have to borrow from {a}.

own_expecting.text: {name} felt the baby stir for the first time while sitting by the fire.
own_expecting.share: I felt the baby stir tonight, sitting by the fire. Just a flutter. I held quite still for an hour.

own_expecting.text: {name} rested every afternoon on the midwife's orders and grumbled about it.
own_expecting.share: The midwife says I must rest every afternoon. I am resting. I am not enjoying it.

own_expecting.text: {name} found the smell of the bakery in the mornings suddenly too much to bear.
own_expecting.share: The bakery smell in the mornings, which I used to love, now sends me straight back indoors.

own_expecting.text: {name} sat with feet up of an evening while {a} fussed over the cushions.
own_expecting.share: {a} fusses over my cushions all evening. I have not lifted a finger since supper and I am told this is right.

own_expecting.text: {name} rubbed {a}'s aching back every evening by the fire.
own_expecting.share: {a}'s back aches in the evenings now, so I rub it by the fire until sleep wins.

own_expecting.text: {name} took over hauling the firewood so {a} could rest.
own_expecting.share: I have taken over all the heavy work so {a} can rest. Hauling firewood has never felt so noble.

own_expecting.text: {name} felt the baby kick under {a}'s hand and laughed out loud.
own_expecting.share: Felt the baby kick under my hand tonight. I laughed out loud and {a} told me to hush.

own_expecting.text: {name} walked {a} home from market at a snail's pace, arm in arm.
own_expecting.share: Walked {a} home from market at a snail's pace, arm in arm. Nobody overtook us without smiling.

own_expecting.text: {name} sat up with {a} through a restless night and read aloud until morning came.
own_expecting.share: {a} could not settle last night, so I read aloud until the sky went grey. The baby liked it, I think.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} got the email confirming they had been approved to adopt.
own_adopting.share: we're approved to adopt. officially. {a} read the email out loud four times

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} finished the last stack of adoption paperwork late into the night.
own_adopting.share: finished the adoption paperwork. my hand is a claw. {a} fell asleep on the forms

own_adopting.text: {name} cleaned the whole house before the social worker's home visit.
own_adopting.share: social worker visit tomorrow. i've cleaned the oven. nobody will look in the oven. i cleaned it anyway

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} sat through their final home study interview holding hands under the table.
own_adopting.share: last home study interview done. {a} squeezed my hand so hard under the table i lost feeling

own_adopting.text: {name} jumped every time the phone rang, hoping it was the agency.
own_adopting.share: every time the phone rings i leap like a startled cat. it was the dentist. again

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} wrote the profile letter that birth families would read.
own_adopting.share: wrote our profile letter for the agency. twelve drafts. {a} cut all my jokes. kept one

own_adopting.text: {name}'s oldest friend wrote a glowing reference for the adoption agency.
own_adopting.share: an old friend wrote our adoption reference. it's so kind i read it twice and had to sit down

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} passed their background checks without a hitch.
own_adopting.share: background checks cleared. turns out we're very boring people. perfect for parenting

own_adopting.text: {name} checked email first thing every morning in case there was news of a match.
own_adopting.share: first thing every morning: check email for match news. second thing: try to act normal

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} went to an adoption support group and came home feeling less alone.
own_adopting.share: went to an adoption support group tonight. so many lovely people in the same waiting room as us

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} spent an afternoon at the agency's training session on attachment.
own_adopting.share: agency training today on attachment. {a} took notes. i took notes on {a}'s notes

own_adopting.text: {name} filed every adoption document in a binder that {a} had color-coded.
own_adopting.share: {a} color-coded our adoption binder. it has tabs. it has sub-tabs. i'm in awe and slightly scared

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} met their social worker for coffee and talked about the waiting.
own_adopting.share: coffee with our social worker. she says the waiting is the hardest part. she's not wrong

own_adopting.text: {name} read adoption forums online until {a} gently closed the laptop.
own_adopting.share: read adoption forums for three hours. {a} closed the laptop and handed me soup. fair

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} signed the final forms at the agency and walked out grinning.
own_adopting.share: signed the final forms at the agency. walked out grinning like we'd pulled off a heist. legally

own_adopting.text: {name} kept the phone on loud at all times in case the agency rang.
own_adopting.share: phone is on loud. always. in the bath. in the cinema. the agency could ring any minute

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} heard from the agency that their profile was now being shown to birth families.
own_adopting.share: agency says our profile is out there being seen by birth families now. heart is doing gymnastics

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} completed an infant first-aid course as part of their adoption preparation.
own_adopting.share: did an infant first aid course for adoption prep. we're certified. the practice doll survived

own_adopting.text: {name} wrote a long email to the social worker full of questions and then deleted half of them.
own_adopting.share: wrote the social worker a huge email of questions. deleted half. sent the rest. still too many

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} updated their adoption profile with a new letter about their home.
own_adopting.share: updated our profile letter. added a bit about our garden and {a}'s terrible singing

own_adopting.text: {name} stared at the phone through dinner until {a} turned it face down.
own_adopting.share: {a} has banned the phone from dinner. face down. i can still hear it not ringing

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} renewed their medical forms for the agency.
own_adopting.share: renewed our medicals for the agency. a doctor says we're fit to parent. a doctor. officially

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} heard from the agency that a match might be coming soon.
own_adopting.share: agency says a match could be close. we've been told to stay calm. we have not stayed calm

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} spent an hour in a shop learning how to fit a car seat.
own_adopting.share: spent an hour learning to fit a car seat. it's a puzzle designed by an enemy

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} ordered a stroller online and assembled it in the hallway.
own_adopting.share: built the stroller in the hallway. took two hours. {a} pushed it round the living room for fun

own_adopting.text: {name} downloaded a baby sleep app on their phone and understood none of it.
own_adopting.share: downloaded a baby sleep app. i don't understand it. the baby isn't even here. already behind

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} rehearsed answers for their adoption panel interview the night before.
own_adopting.share: adoption panel tomorrow. {a} and i rehearsed answers in the kitchen like a play. i forgot my lines

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} went before the adoption panel and were approved unanimously.
own_adopting.share: adoption panel approved us. unanimous. i cried in the corridor. {a} cried in the lift

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} set up a baby monitor in the nursery and tested it on each other.
own_adopting.share: testing the baby monitor by whispering to each other from different rooms. it works. we're giggling

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} looked up nearby daycares just in case.
own_adopting.share: looked up daycares just to feel prepared. we're so prepared. there's no baby yet. very prepared

own_adopting.text: {name} took a phone call from the agency in the middle of the supermarket and had to sit on a crate.
own_adopting.share: agency rang while i was in the supermarket. just an update. i still had to sit on a crate of apples

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} sent a thank-you email to every one of their references.
own_adopting.share: sent thank-you emails to all our references. they all replied asking for updates. we're all waiting together

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} filled out a questionnaire about their parenting values for the social worker.
own_adopting.share: filled out a parenting values questionnaire. {a} and i agreed on everything except bedtimes

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} learned about the court steps that would follow a match.
own_adopting.share: learned all about the court steps after a match. more paperwork. we're experts now

own_adopting.text: {name} kept a list of questions for the agency stuck to the fridge.
own_adopting.share: there's a list of agency questions on the fridge now. it's longer than the shopping list

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} got an update from the agency saying they were next in line for review.
own_adopting.share: agency update: we're next in line for review. i've reorganized the nursery twice in celebration

own_adopting.text: {name} joined an online workshop on welcoming a baby through adoption.
own_adopting.share: did an online adoption workshop. cried at slide four. took notes after that

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} met another adoptive family who had been through the same agency.
own_adopting.share: met another family from our agency. their kid showed us their toy dinosaurs. we're even more ready now

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} heard from the social worker that their home study was officially complete.
own_adopting.share: home study officially complete. the social worker said our house felt warm. i'm keeping that word forever

own_adopting.text: {name} reread the adoption application one last time before posting it to the agency.
own_adopting.share: read the adoption application once more before sending. found one typo. {a} says it's fine. it's not fine

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} had their fingerprints taken for the background check.
own_adopting.share: got fingerprinted for the background check. felt like a spy film. a very wholesome spy film

own_adopting.text: {name} asked friends online for their best advice on surviving the adoption wait.
own_adopting.share: asked friends online how they survived the adoption wait. top answer: hobbies. second answer: more hobbies

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} drove past the agency office just to feel closer to the news.
own_adopting.share: {a} and i drove past the agency office tonight. for no reason. just to wave at it

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} heard from the agency that a birth mother had asked to read their profile.
own_adopting.share: agency says a birth mother asked to read our profile. i can't sit still. {a} has baked three cakes

own_adopting.text: {name} saved the agency's number as the very first favorite on the phone.
own_adopting.share: the agency is now my number one favorite contact. above my mother. she doesn't need to know

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} fixed a few details in their paperwork after the social worker spotted them.
own_adopting.share: small edits to our paperwork from the social worker. turns out i wrote my own birthday wrong. great start

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} sat with their social worker and talked through what a match call would feel like.
own_adopting.share: our social worker walked us through what the match call will be like. already nervous about a call that hasn't happened

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} signed up for a parenting class recommended by the agency.
own_adopting.share: signed up for the agency's parenting class. there's homework. i love homework. {a} does not

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} wrote out their daily routine on a form for the home study.
own_adopting.share: had to write out our daily routine for the home study. it's mostly snacks. we made it sound nicer

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} received an email from the agency saying how much the team loved their profile.
own_adopting.share: agency emailed to say everyone loved our profile. i've read it eleven times. {a} has read it twelve

own_adopting.text: {name} read the agency's welcome pack cover to cover.
own_adopting.share: read the agency welcome pack cover to cover. there's a glossary. i'm learning so many acronyms

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} practiced answering the phone calmly in case it was the agency.
own_adopting.share: we practiced answering the phone calmly in case it's the agency. {a} still squeaks on hello

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} made a little welcome book about their home after the social worker suggested it.
own_adopting.share: social worker suggested a little welcome book about our home. ours has a whole page on the cat

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} worked through a series of videos on adoptive parenting.
own_adopting.share: watched a whole series of adoptive parenting videos with {a}. we're experts now. in theory

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} prepared the little room at the end of the hall for a child.
own_adopting.share: the little room is ready. we keep opening the door just to look at it

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} carried a cradle down from the attic and polished it by hand.
own_adopting.share: brought the old cradle down from the attic and polished it all afternoon. it shines now

own_adopting.text: {name} began stitching a patchwork quilt for the child they were waiting for.
own_adopting.share: started a patchwork quilt for the little one. twelve squares done. many many more to go

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} lay awake talking about the child who would one day come to them.
own_adopting.share: stayed up late with {a} talking about the little one who'll come to us. so much love saved up

own_adopting.text: {name} hung a little curtain at the nursery window.
own_adopting.share: hung a little yellow curtain in the nursery window. the whole room glows in the morning

own_adopting.text: {name}'s mother sent a bundle of tiny clothes she had kept for years.
own_adopting.share: my mother sent a bundle of baby clothes she's been saving for years. she's been waiting for this too

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} practiced rocking a bundle of blankets to get the feel of it.
own_adopting.share: practiced rocking a bundle of blankets with {a}. we're very good at it. the blankets are very calm

own_adopting.text: {name} filled a little chest with soft toys and blankets for the child to come.
own_adopting.share: filled the toy chest today. there's a knitted rabbit in there with a very wise face

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} found that the waiting was harder than any of the preparation.
own_adopting.share: turns out the waiting is the hardest part. the room is ready. we're the ones still fidgeting

own_adopting.text: {name} carved a small wooden horse for the child who had not yet arrived.
own_adopting.share: carved a little wooden horse for the baby. one leg is shorter. adds character

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} took advice from friends who had taken in children of their own.
own_adopting.share: friends who took in a little one came over with advice. the main one: sleep now. while you can

own_adopting.text: {name}'s grandmother told stories of the cousins she had raised as her own.
own_adopting.share: my grandmother told me about raising her cousins as her own. she says love just stretches. i believe her

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} set the cradle by the window so it would catch the morning light.
own_adopting.share: moved the cradle by the window to catch the morning sun. {a} says the baby will be a lark. we'll see

own_adopting.text: {name} knitted a small pair of mittens, then another, then another.
own_adopting.share: knitted one pair of baby mittens. then another. i have eleven now. i can't stop

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} lit a candle in the window on the first evening of the waiting.
own_adopting.share: lit a candle in the window tonight. a little welcome for someone who doesn't know us yet

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} argued gently over which of their old childhood toys to keep for the baby.
own_adopting.share: {a} and i debated which childhood toys to keep for the little one. my one-eyed bear stays. non-negotiable

own_adopting.text: {name} wove a small basket to hold the baby's things.
own_adopting.share: wove a basket for the baby's things. it's wonky. it holds stuff. that's all a basket needs to do

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} made up a little bed with clean linen and lavender.
own_adopting.share: made up the little bed with fresh linen and lavender. smells like a meadow in there

own_adopting.text: {name}'s neighbors came by one by one with small gifts for the child to come.
own_adopting.share: the neighbors keep turning up with tiny gifts. we've got four rattles and a hat with ears

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} practiced lullabies together in the evenings.
own_adopting.share: {a} and i are practising lullabies. we harmonise badly. the cat leaves the room

own_adopting.text: {name} counted the days of waiting by tying knots in a length of ribbon.
own_adopting.share: tying a knot in a ribbon for every day of waiting. it's getting long. so is my patience

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} talked about how they would one day tell the child the story of how they became a family.
own_adopting.share: {a} and i talked about how we'll tell the little one our story. it starts with: we wanted you so much

own_adopting.text: {name} embroidered a tiny star on the corner of a baby blanket.
own_adopting.share: embroidered a little star on the baby blanket. took all evening. worth it

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} found themselves pausing at the nursery door every night before bed.
own_adopting.share: every night {a} and i stop at the nursery door before bed. like checking on someone who isn't here yet

own_adopting.text: {name} received a cradle song written out by an old aunt.
own_adopting.share: my old aunt wrote out a cradle song she used to sing. learned the first verse. working on the second

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} kept busy through the long wait by mending everything in the house.
own_adopting.share: keeping busy while we wait. i've fixed every squeaky hinge in the house. it's eerily quiet now

own_adopting.text: {name} sat in the rocking chair in the empty nursery and imagined holding a baby there.
own_adopting.share: sat in the nursery rocking chair tonight just imagining. it's going to be real one day soon

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} built a set of nursery shelves out of old timber.
own_adopting.share: built nursery shelves out of old wood with {a}. one is slightly slanted. everything rolls left. it's fine

own_adopting.text: {name}'s friends promised to bring a feast the day the child arrived.
own_adopting.share: friends have promised a feast the day the baby comes. they might be more excited than us. almost

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} grew restless and rearranged the nursery yet again.
own_adopting.share: rearranged the nursery again. third time this month. waiting does strange things to a person

own_adopting.text: {name} sewed a little cloth rabbit with button eyes.
own_adopting.share: sewed a cloth rabbit with button eyes. {a} says it looks surprised. i say it looks ready

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} took long evening walks to settle their nerves.
own_adopting.share: evening walks with {a} to calm the nerves. we've walked very far. nerves still here

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} gathered tiny clothes in several sizes, not knowing how little the child might be.
own_adopting.share: we have baby clothes in five sizes because we don't know how little the little one will be. ready for anything

own_adopting.text: {name}'s father mended the old family cradle that had rocked three generations.
own_adopting.share: my dad fixed up the family cradle. it's rocked three generations. ours will be the fourth

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} wrote down their hopes for the child in a little book.
own_adopting.share: {a} and i started a book of hopes for the little one. page one: that you'll feel at home here

own_adopting.text: {name} woke at dawn certain that this would be the day the news came.
own_adopting.share: woke at dawn sure today's the day. it wasn't. but one day it will be, and i'll be up early for it

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} picked wildflowers and dried them to hang over the cradle.
own_adopting.share: dried wildflowers to hang over the cradle. the nursery smells like summer now

own_adopting.text: {name} practiced folding and pinning cloth diapers until it felt natural.
own_adopting.share: practiced folding cloth diapers all evening. i'm now faster than {a}. they want a rematch

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} bickered fondly over who would get to hold the baby first.
own_adopting.share: {a} and i are arguing over who holds the baby first. we're going to flip a coin. best of nine

own_adopting.text: {name}'s elder sister gave a long speech about patience along with a basket of baby things.
own_adopting.share: my sister gave me a long speech about patience and a basket of baby things. took the basket. working on the patience

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} stocked a shelf with soft foods for a child of any age.
own_adopting.share: stocked a shelf of soft foods for the little one. we don't know their age yet so we have all of them

own_adopting.text: {name} caught themself singing to the empty cradle one quiet evening.
own_adopting.share: caught myself singing to the empty cradle tonight. {a} joined in. we're very ready

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} listened to an old friend describe her first week with the foster son she raised.
own_adopting.share: an old friend told us all about her first week with her foster son. we laughed a lot. less scared now

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} finished the nursery and stood in the doorway hand in hand.
own_adopting.share: the nursery is finished. {a} and i just stood in the doorway holding hands. it's ready. we're ready

own_adopting.text: {name} tied a little bell on a ribbon beside the cradle.
own_adopting.share: tied a little bell on a ribbon by the cradle. i keep ringing it. the baby will have to fight me for it

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} settled which of them would take the first night watch.
own_adopting.share: {a} and i decided who gets first night watch. i won. or lost. depends how you look at it

own_adopting.text: {name} could not stop buying tiny socks at the market.
own_adopting.share: bought more tiny socks at the market. that's twenty pairs. i'm not stopping

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} spent the waiting season learning to bake bread together.
own_adopting.share: learning to bake bread while we wait. today's loaf could stop a door. tomorrow's will be better

own_adopting.text: {name} wrote the child a letter to keep until they were grown.
own_adopting.share: wrote a letter for the little one to read when they're grown. it's mostly about how much we wanted them

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} visited friends with a newborn to practice holding a baby.
own_adopting.share: visited friends with a newborn to practice holding. held her like a fragile egg. she fell asleep. victory

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} painted a small sign of welcome to hang over the nursery door.
own_adopting.share: painted a little welcome sign for the nursery door. letters are a bit uneven. the welcome is sincere

own_adopting.text: {name} leapt up every time someone knocked at the door, hoping for news.
own_adopting.share: every knock on the door and i leap up. so far it's been the neighbor twice and a lost goose once

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} filled the house with plants to make it feel warm and alive.
own_adopting.share: {a} and i brought home so many plants. the house feels alive. the little one will grow up in a jungle

own_adopting.text: {name} spent a whole afternoon choosing the softest blanket at a weaver's stall.
own_adopting.share: spent all afternoon choosing the softest blanket at a weaver's stall. squeezed every one. the weaver was patient

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} reminded each other every evening that the right child would come in time.
own_adopting.share: {a} and i remind each other every night: the right little one will come. we believe it

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} counted the coins in the jar they had been saving for the baby.
own_adopting.share: counted the baby savings jar with {a}. it's mostly small coins. it's a lot of small coins

own_adopting.text: {name} hung a mobile of carved wooden birds above the cradle.
own_adopting.share: hung a mobile of little wooden birds over the cradle. they spin when the window's open. so peaceful

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} went to see the parish clerk about taking in a child.
own_adopting.share: We went to see the parish clerk about taking in a little one. He wrote everything down very slowly.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} told the family they meant to raise a child who needed a home.
own_adopting.share: Told the family we mean to raise a child who needs a home. My aunt cried and then gave advice for an hour.

own_adopting.text: {name}'s cousin wrote of a baby in her village who would need a family.
own_adopting.share: My cousin writes there may be a little one in her village who needs a family. We hardly dare hope.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} made up the cradle though nobody yet knew when the baby would come.
own_adopting.share: We have made up the cradle, though nobody can say when the baby will come. It looks very empty and very hopeful.

own_adopting.text: {name} sewed a small quilt from scraps of the whole family's old clothes.
own_adopting.share: I am sewing a quilt from scraps of the whole family's old clothes, so the baby comes wrapped in all of us.

own_adopting.text: The minister visited {name} and {a} to see that their home was fit for a child.
own_adopting.share: The minister came to look over the house and see we are fit to raise a child. I scrubbed the step three times.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} sat up late wondering who their little one would be.
own_adopting.share: Sat up late with {a} wondering who our little one will be. We have imagined at least nine different babies.

own_adopting.text: {name} asked the oldest woman on the street for advice on raising a baby.
own_adopting.share: I asked the oldest woman on our street for advice. She talked until dark and I wrote it all down.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} heard from the foundling home that a baby might be theirs before long.
own_adopting.share: Word from the foundling home: there may be a baby for us before long. I have read the letter twenty times.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} put by a little money each week for the child to come.
own_adopting.share: We put a little by each week now for the little one. {a} keeps the jar on the high shelf, away from me.

own_adopting.text: {name}'s mother brought out the christening gown every child in the family had worn.
own_adopting.share: My mother brought out the christening gown every child in our family has worn. Our little one will wear it too.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} cleared out the small room and scrubbed it from floor to rafters.
own_adopting.share: Cleared out the small room and scrubbed it from floor to rafters. It is ready for someone very small.

own_adopting.text: {name} knitted little caps in three sizes, not knowing how big the baby would be.
own_adopting.share: I have knitted three little caps in three sizes, because nobody can tell me how big the baby will be.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} wrote to every relation to say a child was coming to them.
own_adopting.share: We have written to every relation to say a child is coming to us. The replies are already coming back, full of advice.

own_adopting.text: The midwife promised {name} and {a} she would look in when the baby came.
own_adopting.share: The midwife says she will look in when the baby comes, to see we are doing things right. I am glad of it.

own_adopting.text: {name} walked past the foundling home and stopped to look up at the windows.
own_adopting.share: Walked past the foundling home today and stood looking up at the windows. Somewhere in there, perhaps.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} settled on a name for a girl and another for a boy.
own_adopting.share: We have a name for a girl and a name for a boy now. We shook hands on it like a bargain.

own_adopting.text: {name}'s friends gathered to hem baby linen for the child to come.
own_adopting.share: My friends came round to hem baby linen tonight. We talked more than we sewed, but it got done.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} heard that the baby they were to raise had been born.
own_adopting.share: We hear the baby we are to raise has been born. Soon now. I keep looking at the door.

own_adopting.text: {name} spent an evening carving a little wooden rattle.
own_adopting.share: Spent the evening carving a wooden rattle. It is lopsided. It rattles. That is all a rattle needs.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} hung a little bell over the cradle.
own_adopting.share: Hung a little bell over the cradle. We ring it every time we pass, to practice.

own_adopting.text: {name} dried a bundle of chamomile for the baby's first bath, as the old women advised.
own_adopting.share: The old women say to bathe a new baby in chamomile water, so I have dried a whole bundle. I take advice from everyone now.

own_adopting.text: {name}'s father built a little stool for the child to come.
own_adopting.share: My father has built a little stool for the baby. It will be years before it gets sat on. He does not care.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} minded a neighbor's baby for an afternoon, for practice.
own_adopting.share: Minded the neighbor's baby for an afternoon, for practice. We kept the baby happy and the baby kept us busy.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} found a cradle at the market with a cracked rocker and mended it.
own_adopting.share: Found a cradle at the market with a cracked rocker. {a} mended it in an evening. Good as new, nearly.

own_adopting.text: {name} practiced swaddling a loaf of bread, to the family's delight.
own_adopting.share: Practised swaddling with a loaf of bread. The family thought it very funny. The loaf was very secure.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} kept a candle in the window on the night word was due.
own_adopting.share: We kept a candle in the window tonight while we waited for word. Silly, maybe. It felt right.

own_adopting.text: {name} stitched an initial on a little blanket, then unpicked it because nobody knew the name yet.
own_adopting.share: Stitched an initial on the little blanket, then unpicked it. We do not know the name yet. Too eager.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} signed the papers at the parsonage with shaking hands.
own_adopting.share: We signed the papers at the parsonage today. My hand shook so much the ink blotted. It still counts.

own_adopting.text: {name}'s friends promised to stand by the family when the child came.
own_adopting.share: Our friends say they will stand by us when the child comes. I believe them. It helps.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} walked the long way home, dreaming of the child to come.
own_adopting.share: Walked the long way home with {a}, talking about the little one. We were very slow and very happy.

own_adopting.text: {name} filled a chest with little clothes passed down through the family.
own_adopting.share: The chest at the foot of our bed is full of little clothes from all over the family. Some are older than I am.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} hung a little gown to air by the fire.
own_adopting.share: Hung the little gown to air by the fire. {a} keeps stopping to look at it.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} spent a whole Sunday painting the small room the color of butter.
own_adopting.share: Spent the whole Sunday painting the small room yellow, like butter. It is the happiest room in the house now.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} gave thanks at supper for the child they had been promised.
own_adopting.share: We gave thanks at supper for the little one we have been promised. Neither of us could finish eating.

own_adopting.text: {name} carried the letter from the foundling home everywhere, gone soft from folding.
own_adopting.share: I carry the letter from the foundling home in my pocket. It is going soft from all the folding.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} set aside the best blanket in the house for the baby.
own_adopting.share: Set aside the best blanket in the house for the baby. {a} says we can make do with the scratchy one. Fair.

own_adopting.text: {name} learned the lullabies {name}'s grandmother used to sing.
own_adopting.share: I have been learning the lullabies my grandmother used to sing. I only half remember the words. The tune is what counts.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} told the children on the street a baby was coming, and were asked a great many questions.
own_adopting.share: Told the children on our street a baby is coming to us. I was asked where from, how big, and whether it bites.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} made a list of everything a baby needs and found they had most of it.
own_adopting.share: Made a list of what a baby needs. We have most of it. We have far too many caps.

own_adopting.text: {name} stood in the doorway of the little room each night before bed.
own_adopting.share: Every night before bed I stand in the doorway of the little room for a minute. Soon there will be someone in it.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} went to the fair and could not stop watching the families with little ones.
own_adopting.share: Went to the fair and could not stop watching the families with little ones. Next year that will be us.

own_adopting.text: {name} wove a basket for carrying the baby to market.
own_adopting.share: Wove a basket for carrying the baby to market. It is sturdy. {a} tested it with a cabbage.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} hung a horseshoe over the door for luck before the child came.
own_adopting.share: Hung a horseshoe over the door for luck. Every bit helps.

own_adopting.text: {name} and {a} took the old rocking chair to the joiner to be mended.
own_adopting.share: The old rocking chair has gone to the joiner to be mended. The baby will need rocking and so will I.

own_baby.text: {child} smiled at {name} for the first time, a real smile and not just wind.
own_baby.share: {child} smiled at me today. a proper one. {a} says it was wind. {a} is wrong

own_baby.text: {child} slept five hours in a row for the first time.
own_baby.share: five hours. {child} slept five whole hours. i woke up in a panic because i felt rested

own_baby.text: {child} rolled from back to front on the blanket in the garden.
own_baby.share: {child} rolled over. just went for it. then looked furious about being on {their} tummy

own_baby.text: {child} found {their} own feet and spent the whole morning holding them.
own_baby.share: {child} discovered feet today. {they} {are} very impressed with them. honestly same

own_baby.text: {child} cut {their} first tooth after three grumpy nights.
own_baby.share: first tooth is through. three nights of yelling for one tiny grain of rice in {their} gum

own_baby.text: {child} laughed out loud when {a} sneezed.
own_baby.share: {a} sneezed and {child} laughed so hard {they} got hiccups. {a} has now sneezed fake about forty times

own_baby.text: {child} tasted mashed carrot for the first time and made a face like a betrayed old man.
own_baby.share: first solid food. mashed carrot. {child} looked at me like i'd insulted {their} family

own_baby.text: {child} grabbed a fistful of {name}'s hair and refused to let go.
own_baby.share: {child} has a grip like a blacksmith. i have a bald patch now. worth it

own_baby.text: {child} sat up on {their} own for a few wobbly seconds.
own_baby.share: {child} sat up by {them}self for about four seconds then tipped over like a sack of flour. so proud

own_baby.text: {child} babbled "dadada" all through breakfast.
own_baby.share: {child} said dadada all morning. {a} is acting like it's a full sentence. it's not. probably

own_baby.text: {child} woke at three in the morning just to chat.
own_baby.share: {child} woke at 3am, not hungry, not wet, just wanted to talk. lovely conversation. i'm dead

own_baby.text: {name} and {a} managed a whole dinner while {child} napped.
own_baby.share: we ate a hot dinner while {child} napped. sitting down. with forks. felt like a holiday

own_baby.text: {child} fell asleep on {name}'s chest and nobody dared move for two hours.
own_baby.share: {child} fell asleep on me. i've been pinned for two hours. this is my life now and i accept it

own_baby.text: {child} met {their} grandmother and stared at her earrings for ten straight minutes.
own_baby.share: {child} met my mother today. {they} ignored her completely and fell in love with her earrings

own_baby.text: {child} started crawling backwards and kept ending up under the sofa.
own_baby.share: {child} can crawl. backwards only. keeps reversing under the sofa and getting cross about it

own_baby.text: {child} pulled up to standing against the side of the cradle.
own_baby.share: {child} pulled up to standing in the cradle this morning and looked so smug about it

own_baby.text: {child} took {their} first two steps between {name} and {a} in the kitchen.
own_baby.share: first steps. two of them. between me and {a} in the kitchen. then sat down like nothing happened

own_baby.text: {child} had a blowout so dramatic it reached {their} shoulders.
own_baby.share: we had an incident. up the back. to the shoulders. how. {child} was delighted throughout

own_baby.text: {child} discovered blowing raspberries and did it during {their} bath.
own_baby.share: {child} learned raspberries. bath time is now a spitting contest and i'm losing

own_baby.text: {child} figured out how to clap and clapped at everything.
own_baby.share: {child} can clap now. claps at the dog, claps at the kettle, claps when i trip. supportive

own_baby.text: {child} screamed with joy at the sight of a pigeon.
own_baby.share: {child} saw a pigeon and screamed like it was a celebrity. the pigeon was unbothered

own_baby.text: {name} sang the same lullaby eleven times before {child} gave in.
own_baby.share: eleven rounds of the same lullaby tonight. i don't even know the second verse, i just hum

own_baby.text: {child} slept through the night and {a} checked on {them} four times anyway.
own_baby.share: {child} slept through. {a} did not, because {a} kept checking {they} {were} still breathing

own_baby.text: {child} tried mashed peas and wore most of them.
own_baby.share: peas today. some went in. most went on {their} face, the chair, the wall, and somehow my ear

own_baby.text: {child} recognized {their} name and turned around when {a} said it.
own_baby.share: {child} turned when {a} said {their} name. like {they} knew. i think {they} know

own_baby.text: {child} pulled off one sock and threw it with great intent.
own_baby.share: {child} has started removing socks and throwing them. we've lost nine. {they} {are} building an army somewhere

own_baby.text: {child} giggled every time {name} pretended to eat {their} toes.
own_baby.share: i pretend to eat {child}'s toes and {child} loses it every time. i will do this forever

own_baby.text: {child} had {their} first proper bath in the big tub and kicked water everywhere.
own_baby.share: first big bath. {child} kicked so much water the floor needed mopping. absolute menace

own_baby.text: {name} accidentally put the diaper on backwards at four in the morning.
own_baby.share: put {child}'s diaper on backwards at 4am. {they} didn't care. i cared. i'm a professional

own_baby.text: {child} got the hiccups and found them hilarious.
own_baby.share: {child} had hiccups and laughed at every single one. hiccup, giggle, hiccup, giggle. very efficient

own_baby.text: {child} reached for {a} and said something that sounded a lot like "mama".
own_baby.share: {child} might have said mama. or it was a burp. {a} has decided it was mama

own_baby.text: {child} started teething and chewed on everything within reach.
own_baby.share: teething is here. {child} has chewed my knuckle, the cot rail, and the cat's tail. the cat is filing a complaint

own_baby.text: {child} rolled all the way across the rug to reach a wooden spoon.
own_baby.share: {child} rolled across the whole rug for a wooden spoon. ignored all the actual toys. spoon is king

own_baby.text: {child} dozed off mid-feed with milk still on {their} chin.
own_baby.share: {child} fell asleep mid-feed with milk on {their} chin. little drunk sailor face. melted

own_baby.text: {name} and {a} argued gently over whose turn it was for the night feed.
own_baby.share: {a} and i had a whispered argument at 2am about whose turn it was. we both went. {child} wanted neither

own_baby.text: {child} grabbed {their} grandfather's beard and pulled with surprising strength.
own_baby.share: {child} grabbed grandad's beard and held on. grandad says {child} will make a fine blacksmith

own_baby.text: {child} watched the leaves move in the garden for half an hour.
own_baby.share: {child} lay under the apple tree watching the leaves for half an hour. most peaceful {child} has ever been

own_baby.text: {child} shrieked with delight at {their} own reflection in the mirror.
own_baby.share: {child} saw {them}self in the mirror and shrieked like {they} met a best friend. very sociable baby

own_baby.text: {child} spat out {their} first taste of mashed pear and then wanted more.
own_baby.share: pear today. {child} spat it out, glared at me, then opened {their} mouth for more. confusing review

own_baby.text: {child} found the cat fascinating and tried to grab its whiskers.
own_baby.share: {child} is in love with the cat. the cat is not in love with {child}. we're keeping them apart

own_baby.text: {name} finally got {child} down for a nap and then couldn't remember what to do with the free time.
own_baby.share: got {child} down for a nap and just stood in the hallway. forgot what people do with free time

own_baby.text: {child} started making a little humming noise while feeding.
own_baby.share: {child} hums while feeding now. little contented hum. i'm fine. i'm not crying. it's allergies

own_baby.text: {child} wore the knitted hat {their} grandmother made and looked like a tiny turnip.
own_baby.share: grandma knitted {child} a hat. {child} looks like a turnip. a beautiful turnip

own_baby.text: {child} discovered {their} voice could go very high and tested it all afternoon.
own_baby.share: {child} found {their} high notes today. glass is in danger. the neighbors know {their} name now

own_baby.text: {child} pushed up on {their} arms during tummy time and looked around like a little seal.
own_baby.share: tummy time went well. {child} pushed up and looked around like a seal surveying the beach

own_baby.text: {child} gummed a crust of bread for an hour with total focus.
own_baby.share: gave {child} a crust to gum. {they} worked on it for an hour like it was a job. very dedicated

own_baby.text: {name} spent the whole day with spit-up on one shoulder and didn't notice.
own_baby.share: i went to the market with spit-up on my shoulder. nobody said anything. parents just nod at each other

own_baby.text: {child} slept in the cradle by the hearth while {name} and {a} read.
own_baby.share: quiet evening. {child} asleep by the fire, {a} and me reading. nobody crying. a rare and holy thing

own_baby.text: {child} let out a belly laugh at the sound of a paper bag crinkling.
own_baby.share: {child} thinks crinkling paper is the funniest thing in the world. we have a new career as comedians

own_baby.text: {child} wriggled out of {their} swaddle like a tiny escape artist.
own_baby.share: {child} broke out of the swaddle again. arms everywhere. we're dealing with a professional

own_baby.text: {child} learned to wave and waved at the wall.
own_baby.share: {child} can wave. waved at {a}, at me, at a wall. very friendly with walls

own_baby.text: {child} slept through a thunderstorm while {name} jumped at every clap.
own_baby.share: huge storm last night. {child} slept through all of it. i jumped every time. who's the baby here

own_baby.text: {child} gave {a} a big slobbery open-mouthed kiss.
own_baby.share: {child} gave {a} a kiss. very wet. no technique. {a} is acting like it was a love letter

own_baby.text: {child} grew out of {their} first sleepsuit overnight.
own_baby.share: {child} outgrew {their} newborn clothes. i packed them away and got weirdly emotional about tiny socks

own_baby.text: {child} pulled {name}'s glasses off and tried to eat them.
own_baby.share: {child} took my glasses and tried to eat them. now everything's smudged and so is my heart

own_baby.text: {child} started scooting across the floor on {their} bottom.
own_baby.share: {child} doesn't crawl, {child} scoots. on {their} bum. at speed. it's very efficient and very funny

own_baby.text: {child} babbled at the cat in what sounded like a serious lecture.
own_baby.share: {child} gave the cat a long lecture in baby. the cat looked guilty. i don't know what it did

own_baby.text: {child} grabbed a spoon from {a} and fed {them}self, mostly the chin.
own_baby.share: {child} grabbed the spoon and fed {them}self. hit {their} mouth about once. very independent though

own_baby.text: {name} got a whole uninterrupted shower for the first time in weeks.
own_baby.share: i had a full shower with nobody crying. i stood there way too long. i think i saw god

own_baby.text: {child} wailed when the neighbor's dog barked, then barked back.
own_baby.share: dog barked at {child}, {child} cried, then {child} barked back. we've reached an understanding
